title: Per-tenant fidelity onboarding and billing playbook
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview:
This playbook defines the recommended onboarding and billing processes for per-tenant fidelity configurations (fidelity = model quality/tiering choices that affect latency, cost, and token consumption accounting). It is intended for product managers, solutions engineers, account managers, and billing engineers executing or supporting customer migrations to fidelity-based consumption.

Goals:
- Provide a repeatable onboarding flow for enabling per-tenant fidelity controls.
- Standardize billing events, invoice line items, and metering labels tied to fidelity.
- Minimize customer disruption during migrations, and provide rollback guidance.
- Establish ownership and observability signals to detect regressions or billing mismatches.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: Hosted and Dedicated customers opting into per-tenant fidelity (not edge or on-prem private installs). Includes SDK/console onboarding and backend billing mappings.
- Audience: Product, Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering (SE), Billing, and Engineering (backend/billing teams).

Definitions:
- Fidelity level: named tier mapping to a model variant + runtime profile (e.g., high, standard, economy).
- Fidelity credit: an accounting unit representing per-token effective cost after quality adjustments and bundling.
- Per-route vs per-tenant: this playbook focuses on tenant-wide fidelity defaults and tenant-scoped overrides; route-level guidance is covered in a companion doc.

Prerequisites before onboarding:
1) Contract amendment or subscription agreement signed with fidelity feature flagged.
2) Tenant feature flag enabled in the control plane and assigned to the customer account.
3) Billing product code and ledger entries created by Finance (see Billing mapping table below).
4) SLOs and observability dashboards provisioned in Console for the tenant.
5) SE run basic compatibility and latency smoke tests for customer traffic shape.

Onboarding flow (step-by-step):
1. Initial intake (SE/CS): collect target fidelity expectations, peak QPS, latency requirements, and any compliance constraints. Capture in onboarding ticket template.
2. Contract & billing prep (Finance): create SKU(s) for the tenant with fidelity flags and assign pricing bands. Communicate invoice example to customer.
3. Control plane enablement (Platform): toggle tenant feature flag and create a default fidelity mapping in the tenant config.
4. Test plan (SE/Eng): run synthetic workloads using customer representative prompts at 10–20% of expected QPS. Verify latency and cost footprints.
5. Canary rollout (Platform): stage a canary where 5% of traffic is routed through the fidelity policy for 48–72 hours. Monitor errors, latencies, and cost-per-token.
6. Telemetry validation (SRE/Observability): validate fidelity-specific metrics: per-fidelity token counts, average latency P50/P95, failure rate, and billing events.
7. Full rollout (SE/Platform): expand to 100% following successful canary and stakeholder signoff.
8. Billing reconciliation (Finance/Billing): first invoice cycle post-rollout reconciled with internal metering; provide customer-facing reconciliation if requested.

Minimum acceptance criteria before full rollout:
- P95 latency within agreed SLO for the fidelity level.
- Error rate delta < 0.5% compared to baseline.
- Metering labels emitted for all requests with fidelity metadata (tenant_id, fidelity_level, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out).
- Billing SKU mapped and test invoice generated.

Billing mapping and invoice examples:
Use consistent SKU and invoice line item patterns. Below is the canonical mapping the Billing team uses for hosted and dedicated tenants.

| Ledger Field | Description | Example value |
|--------------|-------------|----------------|
| product_code | Product-level identifier | RW-INF-STD |
| fidelity_code | Per-tenant fidelity identifier | FID-HIGH, FID-STD, FID-ECO |
| unit | Metering unit | token |
| effective_rate | Post-fidelity multiplier applied to base rate | 1.25x (high), 1.0x (standard), 0.75x (economy) |

Invoice line example (human-readable):
- "Redwood Inference — Tokens (FID-HIGH) — Apr 2026 — 1,234,567 tokens @ $0.0009 (effective) = $1,111.11"

Metering labels and events (required):
- "tenant_id": string
- "fidelity_level": string (e.g., high|standard|economy)
- "model_variant": string
- "tokens_in": integer (as string in logs)
- "tokens_out": integer (as string in logs)
- "route_id": optional string

Console and API examples:
- Console: CS user toggles "Tenant fidelity" in the tenant settings page and picks a default. The Console will surface expected cost delta before applying.

- API example (cURL):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/tenant-123/fidelity \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d '{"default_fidelity":"FID-HIGH","overrides":[],"effective_from":"2026-06-01"}'

Implementation notes for engineering:
- Emit fidelity metadata as dedicated labels in the metrics pipeline (Prometheus labels + structured logs).
- Ensure billing pipeline consumes the same labels (Kafka topic: billing-meters) and includes fidelity_code in each record.
- For Dedicated, include node-level affinity annotations in rollout config to reserve capacity for high-fidelity tenants.

Rollout checklist (pre-100%):
- [ ] Feature flag toggled for tenant in control plane.
- [ ] Billing SKU provisioned and test invoice created.
- [ ] Canary run for minimum 48 hours with observability OK.
- [ ] Customer acknowledges expected cost delta and receives invoice sample.
- [ ] CS completes internal readiness playbook and communicates support plan.

Rollback and mitigation guidance:
1. If latency or error rates exceed thresholds during canary: revert default fidelity to previous state and open an engineering incident.
2. If billing mismatch detected: pause metering for the tenant and create a billing reconciliation ticket; notify customer and Finance immediately.
3. If model-quality regressions observed: pin tenant to a previously verified model_variant and schedule a quality investigation with Applied ML.

Monitoring and alerts (recommended thresholds):
- Metric: fidelity_token_rate (per tenant) — alert if drop > 20% vs expected traffic for 30m.
- Metric: fidelity_latency_p95 — alert if increase > 40% vs baseline for 15m.
- Billing alert: parity_check_failures — any daily mismatch > $100 triggers manual review.

Ownership and escalation matrix:
- Primary owner: Product (Asha Patel) — overall product decisions and escalation.
- SE/CS owner: Solutions Eng (Marco Li) — customer readiness and validation.
- Billing owner: Finance/Billing (Sofia Hernandez) — SKU provisioning and invoice reconciliation.
- Engineering owner: Runtime Billing Team (Ethan Cole) — metering pipelines and labeling.

KPIs to track post-launch (first 90 days):
- Time-to-onboard (days) from signed contract to full rollout (target <= 10 days).
- First-month billing accuracy (target >= 99.5% match to internal meters).
- Customer satisfaction (CSAT) for onboarding (target >= 4.2/5).
- Percentage of tenants migrated with automated rollout (target >= 75%).

Appendix: common troubleshooting playbooks (short):
1) Missing fidelity labels in billing pipeline:
   - Validate agent instrumenting requests (check SDK version).
   - Run ad-hoc reprocessing for missing window via billing replay service.
2) Unexpected cost spike after rollout:
   - Temporarily reduce default_fidelity to lower-tier.
   - Run token audit to check for anomalous sequences or loops.
3) Customer disputes invoice:
   - Open billing dispute workflow and provide token-level CSV for the billing window.
